newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end 1.1 percent down on heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end 1.1 percent down on heavy volume.

text.p: * Wall Street fall undermines already brittle NZ market
* Telecom falls again on heavy volume
* Fletcher stocks weak apart from Building
New Zealand shares tumbled on heavy volume on Friday as Wall Street's sharp fall unsettled an already fragile market.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed 24.39 points or 1.08 percent lower at 2,226.60, its lowest finish since October 10.
"We have a market that is pretty brittle at the moment," said John Rattray, director of equities at Ord Minnett.

He said international investors in New Zealand had turned into net sellers as its comparative advantages were less apparent now than 2-3 years ago. "It doesn't shine out like a beacon as an economy that says 'you must invest in me'."
Rattray said the 160 point drop in the Dow had exacerbated the local market's weakness, but noted that shares had dropped on Thursday even after a slight easing from the Reserve Bank.
Weakness was spread virtually across the board, with Telecom shedding nine cents to $6.29 on heavy volume.
Fletcher Building bucked the trend, gaining seven to $4.32, but the other three Fletcher stocks all fell.
Brokers said the outlook next week would partly hinge on Wall Street's performance.
"I think this market is going through a very awkward stage. Even leaving Wall Street aside, I don't think the outlook for the New Zealand market's particularly good at the moment," Rattray said.
